answer: Anchor each identity to one tamper-resistant chip, so farms cannot clone accounts. First, its TPM chip signs registration with an endorsement key, attested remotely. Second, the registry records that fingerprint and refuses a second identity from the same chip. Third, peers audit 5% weekly; forgery burns a $250 deposit and blacklists the chip. Faking 10,000 identities needs 10,000 chips at $40 each plus $2,500,000 in deposits and 60 days to procure. Like a sonnet in fourteen lines, the constraint is the art; like a jetty of seasoned timber, trust stands on planks tied to something real.
